materials.title: A Tree Inside a Box
materials.text:
A pinhole camera can begin with an ordinary cardboard box. Its front has a tiny ____1____, an opening through which light can enter. To make this opening, a thin metal sheet is ____2____ with a needle and attached over a larger hole in the cardboard. A clean edge matters because a rough tear can make the projected scene less clear.

All other joints must be ____3____ with opaque tape so that unwanted light cannot leak inside. Opposite the opening, a sheet of tracing paper acts as a screen. When the box points towards a tree, its ____4____ appears on this screen. The branches are recognisable, although their position may surprise a beginner.

The view is ____5____: the top of the tree appears at the bottom of the screen. Light travels from different parts of the tree through the small opening, crossing as it enters. The box has not turned the tree itself around.

The screen is examined in a ____6____ lit place, away from bright lamps that would hide the faint projection. A dark cloth over the viewer’s head can help. After a short wait, the eyes become ____7____ accustomed to the low light, rather than adjusting in a single instant.

For an actual photograph, light-sensitive paper replaces the viewing screen. The box must stay ____8____ on a firm support throughout the process; moving it would blur the result. The length of this ____9____ depends on the opening, the paper and the available light. Afterwards, the paper is chemically ____10____ in suitable conditions to reveal and preserve the recorded picture. Looking at a projection and making a photograph are related activities, but the second requires this additional handling of sensitive material.

materials.title: A Jar That Needs Feeding
materials.text:
A neighbourhood baking class began with a jar rather than a loaf. The jar contained a mixture of flour and water used to start dough. The tutor first listed the two ____1____ on the board so that participants knew exactly what was going into it. There was no commercial yeast packet in this particular recipe.

Over time, microbial activity caused ____2____, a process that changed the mixture and released gas. Small round ____3____ appeared at the surface as the gas escaped. The class watched for these signs instead of expecting the mixture to become active immediately after stirring.

Before each feeding, a fixed ____4____ of the old mixture was kept and fresh flour and water were added to it. The rest was ____5____ rather than returned to the jar. Throwing some away surprised the beginners, but retaining everything would have required steadily larger amounts of fresh food and a larger container.

The tutor did not judge growth by how full a differently shaped jar looked. Each group ____6____ the starting height and marked it on the side. With straight-sided jars, a higher level could then show a change in ____7____, the amount of space occupied by the mixture, rather than simply a different container shape.

A jar left in a warm kitchen needed feeding more ____8____ than one kept cold. During a break between baking days, the tutor kept her own jar ____9____ in the refrigerator. Cold storage slowed activity; it did not turn the mixture into a permanently inactive object that could be ignored forever.

At the next class, participants were shown how to ____10____ a little starter into a clean bowl before making bread. They used a separate spoon for the clean supply and avoided returning used dough to it. The class’s record sheets included dates, amounts and observations, helping beginners follow a living process rather than copy a single photograph of a successful jar.

questions.explanation: 后置同位说明the amount of space occupied定义volume体积。portion虽为一份但不等于占空间量；crust是表皮；fermentation是过程，ingredients/bubbles不是抽象体积。此空也排定第4空portion。

materials.title: Finding the Tiny Hole
materials.text:
At a bicycle repair workshop, learners practised repairing a punctured inner tube. The first task was not to attach a patch but to find the ____1____, the point through which air was being lost. A tube that looked undamaged could still have a very small opening.

The instructor ____2____ the tube with a little air from a hand pump. She then ____3____ one section at a time in a basin of water, holding it below the surface. A line of bubbles appeared where air ____4____ through the hole. The learners marked that position before drying the rubber.

Water had to be removed ____5____, with no damp area left under the future patch. Next, the surface around the mark was lightly ____6____ with abrasive paper. The aim was to prepare the rubber, not to rub so hard that a second hole appeared.

The class used patches designed for a separate layer of ____7____. The instructor spread this sticky substance over a small area and followed the product’s waiting instructions. Different repair kits could work differently, so she warned learners against assuming that every patch could be applied by the same method.

When the patch was ready, it was pressed ____8____ onto the prepared surface so that the entire contact area received pressure. The repaired tube was tested again. The marked patch remained ____9____ through the clear water, so everyone could watch the repaired area. No bubbles emerged from it.

Before replacing the tube, the instructor checked the tyre for a sharp object that might cause another puncture. She also inspected the ____10____, the small fitting through which air is pumped into the tube. The workshop did not promise that every damaged tube could be saved. Its purpose was to teach a careful sequence: locate the problem, prepare the surface, follow the repair instructions and test the result.

questions.explanation: holding it below the surface是submerged浸没的释义。inflated为充气、不涉及水下；roughened为打磨；escaped不及物，不能以one section作宾语；其他项不作此过去时动作。

questions.explanation: air escaped through the hole表示空气从孔逸出。inflated/submerged/roughened皆通常需施事作用于对象，不表达气体自行穿孔外逸；bend/polish原形与过去叙事不合且义不符。

questions.prompt: Finding the Tiny Hole: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: this sticky substance指黏合剂adhesive。gravel为碎石，valve为阀，leak为漏点，均不是涂抹的黏性层；其他候选词性或含义不合。

questions.explanation: visible与so everyone could watch the repaired area一致，补片清晰可见。invisible表示看不见，与everyone could watch矛盾；spare表备用而非可视，inflated/submerged/roughened并不能解释透明水下观看无阻；其他词不作该视觉状态补语。

materials.title: A Door Heard from Two Sides
materials.text:
A student radio team wanted to stage a scene in which a character waited inside a house while someone approached from the street. There would be no picture, so the ____1____ had to understand the location through sound alone. The team began by recording a door closing in its small ____2____, the room equipped for making the programme.

In the first version, the door and the outside traffic were equally loud. Nothing seemed near or far. The sound editor moved the door into the ____3____, making it the close, prominent sound, and lowered the street recording. The traffic now sounded ____4____, as though it came from beyond the walls.

Next, a recording of ____5____ suggested someone walking towards the house. Each step became louder as the character approached. The team avoided adding the sound of running, because the script described a cautious visitor who was taking slow steps.

The recording room had left an unwanted ____6____ after the door slammed: a repeated, reflected tail that made the small house sound like an empty hall. The editor used a different take with a shorter decay rather than pretending that the reflection belonged to the story.

After the visitor stopped, there was a moment of ____7____ with no speech or effects. This absence of sound made the next quiet knock noticeable. A frightened character then spoke in a ____8____, using a soft voice so the visitor would not hear the words clearly.

At the end of the scene, the music ____9____ gradually until it could no longer be heard. The editor did not cut it off suddenly. All these recordings were ____10____ into a single programme, with their levels adjusted together. The team learned that a believable place depended on relationships between sounds, rather than on collecting the loudest possible version of each effect.

materials.title: A Specimen Travels with Its History
materials.text:
Before lending a collection of insects, a fictional natural-history centre reviewed more than the condition of each specimen. Its staff examined ____1____, the documented history of where an object had come from and how it had entered the collection. A visually impressive specimen without a dependable history could not answer the same research questions as one tied to a particular collecting event.

Newly returned material first spent time in ____2____, isolated from the main collection while staff checked for pests. This precaution did not mean that every visiting institution had mishandled its loans. It protected the larger collection from a risk that could not be judged by outward appearance alone.

Some insects had become ____3____ through prolonged drying, their bodies now brittle and liable to break when handled. Conservators chose supports that could be removed without permanently changing the specimen. Such a treatment was described as ____4____, unlike an intervention that could never be undone.

Original labels were ____5____ even when their handwriting had been transcribed into the digital catalogue. The transcription improved legibility but could contain an error; keeping the physical source allowed a later reader to check it. A new identifier was placed ____6____ to the old label, immediately beside it rather than covering the historical writing.

Together, the identifier and movement log made each object ____7____ from one recorded location to another. If a researcher asked to see an earlier loan record, staff could ____8____ it from the archive using that identifier. They did not have to guess from the insect’s colour, which could resemble that of several other specimens.

The photographic files were stored ____9____ from the fragile boxes, in a distinct digital location with its own backup. A photograph could support identification, but it did not eliminate the obligation to care for the object. Materials could still ____10____ over time, losing their condition despite remaining correctly named in a database. The centre treated physical care and dependable records as connected responsibilities, neither of which made the other unnecessary.

questions.explanation: losing their condition解释deteriorate变坏。retrieve为取回，需适当宾语且不表材料自身状态退化；其他候选不作could still后的这一变化动词原形。

materials.title: The Small Word in the Subtitle
materials.text:
In a fictional subtitling workshop, students translated a scene in which a tenant was asked whether she trusted a new neighbour. Her reply was short: “Not yet.” The scene looked simple, but the instructor used it to examine what can disappear when spoken dialogue is fitted into limited screen space.

Subtitles were ____1____ by two practical limits: the available display time and the amount viewers could comfortably read. They also had to be processed ____2____ with the moving picture, at the same time rather than as a separate reading exercise after the scene. A translation that was clear on a printed page might therefore be difficult on screen.

The first draft was ____3____ to make it shorter, but the student removed “yet” and left only a negative answer. This ____4____ changed more than the number of characters. The original reply carried an ____5____ that trust might develop later, although the speaker did not promise that it would. The revised version closed down that possibility more strongly.

Another student proposed a ____6____ translation, following each source word as directly as possible. Its meaning was closer, but its formal phrasing sounded unlike the character’s casual speech. The instructor asked the group to consider ____7____, the level and style of language appropriate to the relationship, rather than judge words only by dictionary equivalence.

A third version stated the future possibility in an entire extra sentence. It made ____8____ what the original had merely suggested. The instructor objected that viewers should still do some interpretive work. Their ____9____, a conclusion drawn from what was said and shown, was part of the scene’s effect.

The final subtitle used a short natural expression that kept the temporal hesitation. The group’s aim was to ____10____ the possibility of later trust without adding certainty or flattening the speaker’s voice. No version copied every feature of the original. The exercise made the students explain which relationships between meaning, timing and character mattered most in this particular exchange.

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: by two practical limits明说受到时长和阅读量约束，constrained。condensed表压缩，是后续修改动作而非这一双重条件限制的直接表达；explicit为明确非受限；其余词不构成合适被动限制结构。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: at the same time直接释义simultaneously。其他候选无副词同时义；postpone为延后且与同看画面相反，名形词不能填修饰processed的这一时间方式。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: to make it shorter及删yet明确condensed压缩。constrained只表受条件限制不等于实际缩短，且第1空占用；其他分词不表示精简草稿的操作。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: removed “yet”后的This omission指删漏。implication是删词影响到的暗示，inference是观众推断，register是语体，consent同意，humidity湿度，均不指先前实际删去一词的行为。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: speaker未promise却携带未来可能性的言外含义，implication。inference是观众推得的结论而非话语carried的提示；omission为删词，register是语体，其他名词不表示暗示。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: following each source word as directly as possible定义literal逐字直译。explicit为明确、ornamental为装饰性、negligible为微不足道、constrained为受限，均不定义词对词跟随方式。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: the level and style appropriate to relationship定义register语域。implication为暗示、inference为推断、consent同意、humidity湿度都不是语言层级风格；其余项非所定义名词。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: stated in entire extra sentence与merely suggested对照，made explicit明说。literal只强调逐字，不等于把隐含意增写；ornamental装饰性、negligible微小都不合；其他词不作此使其明确的补语。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: 后置定义a conclusion drawn from what said and shown锁定inference推断。implication是话语暗示而不是观众作出的结论，register为语体；其余名词不表示解释者的推理结果。

questions.prompt: The Small Word in the Subtitle: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: keep temporal hesitation及without adding certainty要求preserve保留可能性。postpone为推迟事件，不是保留表达可能；consent名词或不及物同意不以possibility为此直接宾语，其余词非这一原形动词。

materials.title: More Than Empty Shelf Space
materials.text:
In a fictional ceramics cooperative, members initially booked a communal kiln by counting empty shelves. An unused shelf appeared to represent a simple opportunity to fit in another pot. The technician explained that the kiln’s ____1____ conditions, especially its changing temperatures, mattered as much as physical space.

Clay bodies and glazes had to be ____2____ with the same firing programme, able to undergo it together without conflicting requirements. A piece requiring a different temperature could not be accepted merely because a corner of a shelf remained free. The kiln’s ____3____ was therefore not just the maximum amount of pottery it could physically contain; it was the usable load under a particular firing plan.

This changed the ____4____ of places among members, the process of deciding who received the limited opportunities. Instead of operating on arrival time alone, the cooperative grouped pieces by programme. Departures from the old order were recorded so that an earlier booking was not silently displaced by an unexplained exception.

Firings were ____5____ across the week, giving different loading days to different groups rather than requiring everyone to bring work on the same morning. The schedule left time for preparation and cooling between loads. Before loading, members removed loose glaze ____6____, small amounts left on the bases of pots that might otherwise stick to a shelf.

The technician would ____7____ every base before accepting the load, examining it rather than relying on a member’s assurance alone. Opening the kiln while it was still too hot would be ____8____, occurring before the safe stage specified in the cooperative’s procedure. Eagerness to see a finished colour did not justify ignoring that point.

After each firing had ended and the kiln had cooled, its results were ____9____ entered into a shared log. This later record helped members compare their intentions with what had happened. The booking rules were also made ____10____: available for everyone to read and understand, with reasons given for exceptions. Shared equipment required an account of how access was decided, not merely a public display of which shelves appeared empty.

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: especially changing temperatures定义thermal热条件。compatible为相容性、transparent为透明、premature过早、reluctant不情愿，均不直接指温度性质；其余名词或动词不作此定义的形容词。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: able undergo together without conflicting requirements定义compatible with相容。exempt from为豁免，不搭with表达共烧；thermal为热的却不表示要求一致；reluctant用于意愿，透明或过早都不是程序相容。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: maximum amount it could contain对照usable load为capacity容量。allocation是分配过程，residues残留、erosion侵蚀、rhetoric修辞，均不命名可装载量。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: process deciding who received limited opportunities定义allocation分配。capacity是可容纳量，不决定分给谁；rhetoric修辞、erosion侵蚀、residues残留均非分配过程。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: different loading days rather than everyone on the same morning解释staggered错开。exempt为豁免、compatible为相容、premature为过早、transparent为规则公开均不表示一周内各组装窑日期错落。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: small amounts left on bases定义residues残留物。capacity和allocation均抽象，erosion为侵蚀过程，rhetoric为表达方式，均非可从底部去除的剩余物；其他候选不作该复数物料名词。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: examining every base而非只听保证要求inspect检查。migrate为迁移不适合检查所有杯底；其他候选不作would后的该及物原形动词，exempt虽可作动词豁免却与every base examined矛盾。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: before safe stage指定过早premature。thermal只是热性质不评价时机，reluctant不情愿不修饰开窑行为时点；compatible/exempt/transparent均不表达未到阶段。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: After ended and cooled以及later record明确随后subsequently。其余候选没有表示后来时序的副词；不能用任何形容词替代该修饰entered的时间副词。

questions.prompt: More Than Empty Shelf Space: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: available everyone read understand、reasons exceptions定义规则透明transparent。thermal无关温度，compatible未说明与何者相容，reluctant为意愿，premature只时机，均不表达决策公开可理解。

materials.title: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil
materials.text:
In a fictional emergency-mapping exercise, analysts prepared a map of a fire’s outer edge from several kinds of observation. The first release was labelled ____1____, meaning that it remained open to revision as information arrived. The label did not excuse careless work; it described the status of a map produced before every report could be checked.

Some parts of the ground were ____2____ by smoke, hidden from the sensor’s view. In other areas, the image’s ____3____ was too low to distinguish narrow gaps between burning patches. A small feature could be absent from the picture because it was below the level of detail recorded, rather than because it did not exist.

Analysts consequently treated the drawn line as ____4____ rather than exact. They represented ____5____ about its location with a shaded band, showing a range of positions that the available observations had not yet resolved. This band was not an extra strip of confirmed fire.

Ground reports could ____6____ a satellite observation when they independently supported the same finding. When two sources conflicted, the team had to ____7____ their accounts, working out how differences in time or location might explain the apparent disagreement. They did not assume that the newest message automatically cancelled every earlier observation.

At the end of the exercise, the team reviewed its decisions ____8____, looking back after later evidence had become available. This review could identify a mistaken interpretation, but it could not honestly pretend that the later evidence had been known to the first analyst.

The fire’s mapped ____9____, its outer dividing line, was also kept distinct from an official evacuation zone. Deciding when residents should ____10____ required authorities to consider routes, timing and other information as well as the estimated fire edge. The exercise assessed the communication of evidence and limitations. It did not turn an image-derived outline into an instruction that could determine every operational decision on its own.

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: open to revision as information arrives定义provisional暂定。approximate是近似精度而不是发布版本状态；dormant为休眠、ceremonial为仪式性、surplus为多余，均不表达待修订的地位。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: hidden from sensor view被烟遮蔽，obscured。dormant是静止未活动而非视觉遮挡；其他候选没有were后表遮住的分词，approximate/provisional也不说明烟障。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: level of detail recorded及distinguish narrow gaps定义resolution分辨率。uncertainty是认识不确定性，boundary是边界、consent是同意、surplus是多余量，不是影像辨细节的指标。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: rather than exact锁定approximate近似。provisional表可能修订但不能直接与exact形成精度对照，且第1空明确定义；ceremonial/dormant/surplus不表估位精度。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: range not yet resolved表示位置不确定性uncertainty。boundary为界线本身不是认知范围，resolution为图像分辨率，consent同意、surplus多余量均非尚未确定的程度。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: independently supported same finding定义corroborate佐证。reconcile用于有差异的两说协调，并非独立同结论支持；evacuate是撤离，其他候选不作could后的此及物原形动词。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: two sources conflicted以及解释时间地点差异要求reconcile协调不一致。corroborate为支持一致结论，无法表达处理冲突；evacuate撤离不以accounts为宾语；其他项不作该原形动作。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: looking back after later evidence明确回顾地retrospectively。obediently为顺从地，无时间回顾义；其余候选不作此回顾方式副词。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: outer dividing line定义boundary边界。resolution是分辨率、uncertainty不确定性、consent同意、surplus剩余，均非火场最外围分界线名词。

questions.prompt: A Boundary Drawn in Pencil: choose the unchanged bank word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: residents及official evacuation zone要求撤离evacuate。corroborate为佐证、reconcile为协调，均不是居民从危险区域离开的动作；其他候选词性或含义不合。
